changes: Weekday normalised: 'roja 7 vāla' = 7th day, i.e. Saturday (roja = day); recorded as '7 (Saturday)' rather than 'roja 7'.
as_written for Kāśīnātha trimmed to the form as it appears (kāśinātha-), without śrī; stem normalised to Kāśīnātha.
Scribe confidence lowered to medium because the instrumental keśavasiṃhana stands next to the unclear 'dai iba bhe' and the clause only says the book was completed by him.
Date: the dated clause is still read as NS (century omitted) 28. The notes now explain the conflict with the catalogue's NS 591 (= 1471 CE) and give possible ce values.

persons.name: Keśavasiṃha
persons.evidence: thva saphūlasidha yakā dina juro || || dai iba bhe || keśavasiṃhana juro

notes: The catalogue gives NS 591 (= 1471 CE), probably from the bare number '591' right after the text's closing words. That number has no 'samvat' and could instead be a grantha/verse count. The full date with tithi and weekday is 'samvat 28 pauṣa śukla 12, Saturday', which seems to have the century left out (e.g. NS 728 = 1608 CE or NS 828 = 1708 CE). The Persian loan 'roja' (day) and the Newari wording suggest the later Malla period rather than 1471, so ce_approx is left empty. If 591 is the year, the copy dates to 1471 CE. A weekday check of Pauṣa śu. 12 against NS 591 and 728/828 could settle this. 'thva saphū lasidha yakā dina juro' = 'this is the day the book was completed'. 'dai iba bhe' is unclear (perhaps corrupt; maybe a title like daivajña, or a place or a relative). Keśavasiṃha is taken as the scribe on the strength of the instrumental 'keśavasiṃhana juro', as the catalogue also has it.
